request.what: Withdraw treasury funds for Intersect Technical Steering Committee Support covering 12 months of community engagement, protocol governance, and independent technical review activities.

claims.claim: Intersect requests $298,250, stated as 1,193,000 ADA, to support Technical Steering Committee activities for 12 months.

The requested 1,193,000 ADA is allocated across three work packages: 256,000 ADA for community-facing technical coordination, 832,000 ADA for protocol governance and evolution, and 105,000 ADA for technical review.
Execution of the listed work packages is contingent on approval of the IntersectMBO budget proposal.

The proposal says the TSC work supports Cardano technical governance by giving community members and DReps information for governance decisions and by making protocol evolution structured, transparent, and accountable.
WP3 independent technical reviews are described as subject to formal conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.
The proposal states it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and links to budget process and audit references.
The proposal asserts that the withdrawal does not, at the time of submission, breach the applicable 350M ADA Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 and links to the referenced governance action.
Independent audits and assurance for this proposal are stated to be provided by Appold, with possible reviews of deliverable verification, control testing, spend validation, and milestone evidence.

The proposal discloses that the Technical Steering Committee has not received Cardano Treasury funding in the past 24 months, while Intersect and its committees have received 22,385,000 ADA through listed prior governance actions.

Intersect states the funds will be managed through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, named oversight entities, threshold permissions, and a public dashboard for auditability.

summary: The document requests 1,193,000 ADA for 12 months of TSC support across three work packages, with stated smart-contract custody, oversight, assurance, prior-funding disclosure, and NCL compliance, but the deterministic assessment records missing budget, feasibility, risk, alternatives, and failure-mode analysis.
